title: Truganini
summary: Truganini, a Palawa woman of Tasmania, was born on Bruny Island about 1812 and died in Hobart in 1876. After her death her remains were put on display at the Tasmanian Museum. In 1976 her ashes were scattered on the waters of the D'Entrecasteaux Channel.

uncertainty.note: Both opened pages say she was born "about" or "around" 1812.

where.modern_name: Bruny Island, Tasmania, Australia; pinned to her birthplace and homeland (she died in Hobart)
where.historical_name: Bruny Island, Van Diemen's Land (British colony)

importance.justification: Her life and the museum display of her bones after death are widely told in Australian museum histories of Tasmanian Aboriginal people.

audience_note: Includes the display of a Tasmanian Aboriginal woman's remains as a museum specimen, a subject that may distress Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander viewers.

reviewer_note: Spelling varies; the National Portrait Gallery notes Trukanini is the spelling used by the Palawa people. Review wording with Aboriginal community guidance. 2026-11-03: the Australian Museum page is gone with no archived copy, so it was replaced by the Australian Women's Register. The end date of the display was dropped: 1947 rested on the lost page, and the Register gives 1904 to 1907.
